blocks.prompt: 3 (i) Find the angle from line \(\ell_1\) to the line \(\ell_2\), where \(\ell_1\): \(2x + y - 3 = 0\); \(\ell_2\): \(x + y - 5 = 0\).
blocks.explanation:
Is dafa lines points se nahi balke equations se di gayi hain, general form \(ax + by + c = 0\) mein.
Is form mein slope \(m = -\frac{a}{b}\) hota hai, yani \(x\) ka coefficient over \(y\) ka coefficient, minus ke saath.
Dono slopes nikal kar Theorem 7 lagayenge, \(\ell_1\) se \(\ell_2\) tak.
Plan: slopes, formula, angle.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\ell_1: 2x + y - 3 = 0\), \(\ell_2: x + y - 5 = 0\).
Maloom karna: \(\ell_1\) se \(\ell_2\) tak angle \(\theta\).
Tareeqa: \(ax + by + c = 0\) ka slope \(-\frac{a}{b}\); phir Theorem 7.

Slopes nikalein
\[m_1 = -\dfrac{2}{1} = -2\]
\[m_2 = -\dfrac{1}{1} = -1\]
Kyun: \(y\) ke liye hal karein to \(y = -2x + 3\) aur \(y = -x + 5\); \(x\) ka coefficient hi slope hai. Formula \(-\frac{a}{b}\) isi ka shortcut hai.

Theorem 7 lagayein
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{-1 - (-2)}{1 + (-2)(-1)}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{3}\]
Kyun: \(m_2\) pehle; \(-1 + 2 = 1\) aur \((-2)(-1) = 2\), is liye neeche \(1 + 2 = 3\).
Dhyan dein: \(-(-2)\) ko \(+2\) banana na bhoolein.

Angle parhein
\[\theta = \tan^{-1}\tfrac{1}{3} = 18.43^\circ\]
Kyun: tan positive hai, is liye angle acute.

Tasdeeq:
Inclinations se: \(\tan^{-1}(-1)\) se \(135^\circ\) aur \(\tan^{-1}(-2)\) se \(116.57^\circ\).
\[135^\circ - 116.57^\circ = 18.43^\circ \;\checkmark\]
Yeh wahi \(\theta = \alpha_2 - \alpha_1\) hai jo Theorem 7 ke proof mein tha.
Do tareeqon se ek hi jawab aaya, is liye ab poora yaqeen hai.

blocks.prompt: 3 (ii) Find the angle from line \(\ell_1\) to the line \(\ell_2\), where \(\ell_1\): \(2x - 3y + 2 = 0\); \(\ell_2\): \(x + y - 4 = 0\).
blocks.explanation:
Phir general form, har line ka slope \(-\frac{a}{b}\).
\(\ell_1\) mein \(b = -3\) hai, sign ka khaas khayal rakhna hai.
Theorem 7 lagayenge; tan negative aaya to angle obtuse.
Plan: slopes, formula, angle.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\ell_1: 2x - 3y + 2 = 0\), \(\ell_2: x + y - 4 = 0\).
Maloom karna: \(\ell_1\) se \(\ell_2\) tak angle \(\theta\).
Tareeqa: slopes \(-\frac{a}{b}\), phir Theorem 7.

Slopes nikalein
\[m_1 = -\dfrac{2}{-3} = \dfrac{2}{3}\]
\[m_2 = -\dfrac{1}{1} = -1\]
Kyun: \(\ell_1\) mein \(a = 2\), \(b = -3\); minus over minus plus.
Dhyan dein: bohat se bachay yahan \(-\frac{2}{3}\) likh dete hain; \(b\) ka sign saath lena zaroori hai.

Theorem 7 lagayein
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{-1 - \frac{2}{3}}{1 + \frac{2}{3}(-1)}\]
\[= \dfrac{-5/3}{1/3} = -5\]
Kyun: \(-1 - \frac{2}{3} = -\frac{5}{3}\) aur \(1 - \frac{2}{3} = \frac{1}{3}\); \(\frac{1}{3}\) se divide karna 3 se multiply karna hai.

Angle parhein
\[\tan^{-1} 5 = 78.69^\circ\]
\[\theta = 180^\circ - 78.69^\circ = 101.31^\circ\]
Kyun: tan negative hai, angle obtuse; positive value ka angle \(180^\circ\) mein se minus kiya.
